# gh-1420: [feat] merge-hold observability + post-merge sweep coverage for unresolved threads

## Description

## Problem

1. The only evidence that the PR #1410 merge was wrong sat in a runner log line nobody watches:
   `🧵 merge backstop … (1 open human thread(s) stay per gh-744) — merge as today`
   (run 42647579054, 2026-11-09T15:44:01Z). Misclassifications, holds and policy downgrades are invisible at the PR/repo level.
2. The open thread on PR #1410 (IMPORTANT, created 2026-11-09T15:42:42Z) remains **unresolved days after the merge** — the gh-1379 post-merge sweep did not pick it up (precedent: PR #1386, "Post-merge sweep: 2 unresolved threads"). Why it was missed needs a root cause: likely the same author-allowlist blindness or a trigger-scope gap. An unresolved machine review thread on a merged PR is exactly the debt the digest/ledger machinery was built to never lose.

## Design

a. **Merge-decision markers (rides the verdict-freshness (#1416) and open-discussion-gate (#1417) issues):** every deferred merge refreshes the `dmtools:merge-hold` marker comment on the PR (reason, counts, head — one comment per head). This issue adds the **funnel-side summary marker** when a merge happens despite the backstop having counted anything:
   `dmtools:merge-note {"openThreadsAtMerge":N,"autoResolved":K,...}` — so "merged with residue" is visible in the PR timeline, not only in logs. Deduped per head; comment-reduction doctrine applies.

b. **Log format v2 for the funnel:** one greppable structured line per decision:
   `MERGE-DECISION pr=1410 head=0c2732d action=merged|held|deferred machineThreads=N humanThreads=H allowlist=len verdict=<newest|none>`
   — makes both the misclassification (`allowlist=0`) and holds greppable across runs; keep the legacy human-readable lines for the backstop's `say()` output.

c. **Post-merge sweep coverage:** extend the gh-1379 sweep so every merged PR with unresolved machine-authored review threads gets the digest treatment (gh-1353 ledger identity — same file+claim+severity key, so pre-merge digests and post-merge sweep converge on one entry), and unresolved human threads on merged PRs are listed in the same digest as `open (human)`. Test case: PR #1410's thread must be picked up by the sweep on its next run after this ships. Root-cause FIRST why the current sweep missed it (check: author allowlist in the sweep's context, event triggers, severity filter) and record the cause in this issue before the fix merges.

d. **Optional:** a workflow-level `::warning::` annotation on holds so the Actions UI surfaces them without reading logs.

## Implementation constraints

- GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, hoisted requires).
- Unit tests with scripted payloads; no dry-run requirement (owner decision 2026-11-05).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Marker comments are machine-parseable, deduped per head (refresh test); no comment is posted when nothing was counted (pure-clean merges stay silent).
2. The structured decision line appears in all three funnels' logs (unit-testable via the shared `say`/logger seam).
3. The sweep, run against a scripted payload shaped like PR #1410, creates ONE digest entry for the unresolved machine thread (idempotent on re-runs — the convergent one-digest-per-PR invariant asserted).
4. The root cause of the gh-1379 miss on #1410 is written into this issue (investigation note) before the sweep fix merges.
5. GraalJS-clean.

Alert routing to external systems (Slack/email — none exists today); the hold machinery itself (verdict-freshness / open-discussion-gate issues).

# gh-1420 — the post-merge thread sweep + merge-decision observability

## Root cause (AC4) — why gh-1410's threads were never swept

**The trigger-scope gap.** The merge-backstop (gh-1353) fires at the merge
instant: it digests the PR's unresolved machine-authored review threads into
the review debt ledger and resolves them. It has no idea the PR's issue even
exists — it never touches the tracker.

The issue-close path (`machineSmAgent.decideActions`, the
`ai_developed → linked PR merged` branch) fires on the *next* tick, when the
merge is already done: for a MERGED PR it planned exactly one action —
`closeIssue` (the "Fixes #N safety net"). `closeIssue` closes the tracker
issue and stops. **No step between the merge and the close ever looked at the
PR's review threads**, and no later tick ever looks at a PR again (the SM
loop is issue-driven; merged issues are terminal). So a machine thread that
the backstop could not resolve (its `deferred:` ledger append failed), or a
human thread it deliberately left open, stayed unresolved on a merged,
closed-forever PR — exactly gh-1410: PR merged, issue closed, thread open,
nobody scheduled anything.

Three contributing gaps, same root:

1. **The pre-merge gates had no residue record.** When the backstop deferred
   a machine thread at the merge instant, the merge still proceeded (by
   design — the debt is ledgered), but nothing on the PR recorded that it
   merged with open threads. The merge-note marker (`dmtools:merge-note`)
   did not exist.
2. **The merge decision was unobservable.** A merged PR and a held PR
   produced the same log shape (`result.merged: 1` / `result.skipped: 1`
   plus prose), so a held merge was invisible in Actions logs and gh-1410's
   "why did this merge with a thread open" question had no greppable answer.
3. **The sweep depended on a re-visit that never comes.** gh-1420's draft
   (`postMergeSweep.runSweep`) existed but nothing invoked it: its natural
   trigger — the merged-PR close tick — is also the *only* tick on which the
   PR's issue is still open, and that tick closed the issue without sweeping.

## The fix

1. **`postMergeSweep` wired into the close tick** (`machineSmAgent`): a MERGED
   PR now plans `[mergedThreadSweep, closeIssue]` — the sweep rides the close
   tick (the only tick the issue is open), fail-soft: any sweep error is
   swallowed and the close always proceeds. The sweep digests unresolved
   machine threads into the review debt ledger (the gh-1353 identity —
   convergent, one entry per finding) under the canonical
   `deferred: <findingId>` disposition, resolves them on success, and lists
   unresolved human threads `open (human)` in the same digest. Digest
   comments dedupe per PR (`dmtools:post-merge-sweep` marker, digest hash).
2. **The merge-note marker (AC1)** — `common/mergeNote.js`, appended to all
   three funnels (`mergeTrigger`, `mergeBot`, `retryMergeGithubPR`): when the
   merge-backstop counted residue (`openThreadsAtMerge > 0`), the merged PR
   gets ONE `<!-- dmtools:merge-note {...} -->` comment with the open/auto-
   resolved counts, the resolved finding ids, and the head sha. One note per
   head (deduped), never on a clean merge, never on a held merge, wrapped in
   `<details>` so review-thread re-reads ignore it.
3. **The structured merge-decision line (AC2, design-d)** — every funnel says
   `MERGE-DECISION pr=N head=<7> action=merged|held|defered
   machineThreads=N humanThreads=N allowlist=N verdict=<WORD|none>` at
   decision level, plus a `::warning:: MERGE-HELD pr=N reason=…` annotation
   line on holds so the Actions UI surfaces them.

  registered in `run_all.json`.
- Emission suites: `test_mergeTrigger.js` +6, `test_mergeBot.js` +4,

# gh-1420: [feat] merge-hold observability + post-merge sweep coverage for unresolved threads

## Description

## Problem

1. The only evidence that the PR #1410 merge was wrong sat in a runner log line nobody watches:
   `🧵 merge backstop … (1 open human thread(s) stay per gh-744) — merge as today`
   (run 42647579054, 2026-11-09T15:44:01Z). Misclassifications, holds and policy downgrades are invisible at the PR/repo level.
2. The open thread on PR #1410 (IMPORTANT, created 2026-11-09T15:42:42Z) remains **unresolved days after the merge** — the gh-1379 post-merge sweep did not pick it up (precedent: PR #1386, "Post-merge sweep: 2 unresolved threads"). Why it was missed needs a root cause: likely the same author-allowlist blindness or a trigger-scope gap. An unresolved machine review thread on a merged PR is exactly the debt the digest/ledger machinery was built to never lose.

## Design

a. **Merge-decision markers (rides the verdict-freshness (#1416) and open-discussion-gate (#1417) issues):** every deferred merge refreshes the `dmtools:merge-hold` marker comment on the PR (reason, counts, head — one comment per head). This issue adds the **funnel-side summary marker** when a merge happens despite the backstop having counted anything:
   `dmtools:merge-note {"openThreadsAtMerge":N,"autoResolved":K,...}` — so "merged with residue" is visible in the PR timeline, not only in logs. Deduped per head; comment-reduction doctrine applies.

b. **Log format v2 for the funnel:** one greppable structured line per decision:
   `MERGE-DECISION pr=1410 head=0c2732d action=merged|held|deferred machineThreads=N humanThreads=H allowlist=len verdict=<newest|none>`
   — makes both the misclassification (`allowlist=0`) and holds greppable across runs; keep the legacy human-readable lines for the backstop's `say()` output.

c. **Post-merge sweep coverage:** extend the gh-1379 sweep so every merged PR with unresolved machine-authored review threads gets the digest treatment (gh-1353 ledger identity — same file+claim+severity key, so pre-merge digests and post-merge sweep converge on one entry), and unresolved human threads on merged PRs are listed in the same digest as `open (human)`. Test case: PR #1410's thread must be picked up by the sweep on its next run after this ships. Root-cause FIRST why the current sweep missed it (check: author allowlist in the sweep's context, event triggers, severity filter) and record the cause in this issue before the fix merges.

d. **Optional:** a workflow-level `::warning::` annotation on holds so the Actions UI surfaces them without reading logs.

## Implementation constraints

- GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, hoisted requires).
- Unit tests with scripted payloads; no dry-run requirement (owner decision 2026-11-05).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Marker comments are machine-parseable, deduped per head (refresh test); no comment is posted when nothing was counted (pure-clean merges stay silent).
2. The structured decision line appears in all three funnels' logs (unit-testable via the shared `say`/logger seam).
3. The sweep, run against a scripted payload shaped like PR #1410, creates ONE digest entry for the unresolved machine thread (idempotent on re-runs — the convergent one-digest-per-PR invariant asserted).
4. The root cause of the gh-1379 miss on #1410 is written into this issue (investigation note) before the sweep fix merges.
5. GraalJS-clean.

## Out of scope

Alert routing to external systems (Slack/email — none exists today); the hold machinery itself (verdict-freshness / open-discussion-gate issues).

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Runtime-artifact guard (tracked artifacts / tracked-but-ignored)
        # gh-1365: pipeline-owned runtime artifacts must never be tracked — a modified
        # TRACKED artifact in a runner workspace blocks every dev-leg checkout (the
        # gh-1358/.dmtools-target-workingdir incident), while an untracked+ignored
        # copy is harmless by construction. Both checks are read-only `git ls-files`
        # queries evaluated against the checked-out INDEX — no working-dir state is
        # consulted, so dirty runner workspaces cannot influence the verdict:
        #  1. tracked files matching ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt — the checked-in
        #     gitignore-style list deployments extend WITHOUT touching this workflow;
        #  2. tracked files matching the repo's own ignore rules (`--exclude-standard`)
        #     — the "tracked but ignored" state, i.e. the missed-cleanup signature.
        # Any hit fails the job naming the file and the exact remediation (never just
        # a count); both checks always run so one bad tree reports every violation.
        run: |
          set -e
          patterns="ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt"
          status=0
          report="$(mktemp)"

          hits="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-from="$patterns")"
          if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "Tracked files match \`$patterns\` — runtime artifacts must never be tracked. Untrack each one:"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\` and add the path to .gitignore"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked runtime artifact matches $patterns — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\" and add the path to .gitignore"
              done <<EOF
          $hits
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked file matches \`$patterns\`."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          ignored="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-standard)"
          if [ -n "$ignored" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "These tracked files match the repo's own .gitignore rules but are still tracked (the missed-cleanup signature — untrack so the ignore rule takes effect):"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\`"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked but matches .gitignore — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\""
              done <<EOF
          $ignored
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked-but-ignored files."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          cat "$report"
          cat "$report" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit $status

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |

          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \

            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else

{"body":"## Problem

1. The only evidence that the PR #1410 merge was wrong sat in a runner log line nobody watches:
   `🧵 merge backstop … (1 open human thread(s) stay per gh-744) — merge as today`
   (run 42647579054, 2026-11-09T15:44:01Z). Misclassifications, holds and policy downgrades are invisible at the PR/repo level.
2. The open thread on PR #1410 (IMPORTANT, created 2026-11-09T15:42:42Z) remains **unresolved days after the merge** — the gh-1379 post-merge sweep did not pick it up (precedent: PR #1386, "Post-merge sweep: 2 unresolved threads"). Why it was missed needs a root cause: likely the same author-allowlist blindness or a trigger-scope gap. An unresolved machine review thread on a merged PR is exactly the debt the digest/ledger machinery was built to never lose.

## Design

a. **Merge-decision markers (rides the verdict-freshness (#1416) and open-discussion-gate (#1417) issues):** every deferred merge refreshes the `dmtools:merge-hold` marker comment on the PR (reason, counts, head — one comment per head). This issue adds the **funnel-side summary marker** when a merge happens despite the backstop having counted anything:
   `dmtools:merge-note {"openThreadsAtMerge":N,"autoResolved":K,...}` — so "merged with residue" is visible in the PR timeline, not only in logs. Deduped per head; comment-reduction doctrine applies.

b. **Log format v2 for the funnel:** one greppable structured line per decision:
   `MERGE-DECISION pr=1410 head=0c2732d action=merged|held|deferred machineThreads=N humanThreads=H allowlist=len verdict=<newest|none>`
   — makes both the misclassification (`allowlist=0`) and holds greppable across runs; keep the legacy human-readable lines for the backstop's `say()` output.

c. **Post-merge sweep coverage:** extend the gh-1379 sweep so every merged PR with unresolved machine-authored review threads gets the digest treatment (gh-1353 ledger identity — same file+claim+severity key, so pre-merge digests and post-merge sweep converge on one entry), and unresolved human threads on merged PRs are listed in the same digest as `open (human)`. Test case: PR #1410's thread must be picked up by the sweep on its next run after this ships. Root-cause FIRST why the current sweep missed it (check: author allowlist in the sweep's context, event triggers, severity filter) and record the cause in this issue before the fix merges.

d. **Optional:** a workflow-level `::warning::` annotation on holds so the Actions UI surfaces them without reading logs.

## Implementation constraints

- GraalJS-clean (var + plain functions, hoisted requires).
- Unit tests with scripted payloads; no dry-run requirement (owner decision 2026-11-05).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Marker comments are machine-parseable, deduped per head (refresh test); no comment is posted when nothing was counted (pure-clean merges stay silent).
2. The structured decision line appears in all three funnels' logs (unit-testable via the shared `say`/logger seam).
3. The sweep, run against a scripted payload shaped like PR #1410, creates ONE digest entry for the unresolved machine thread (idempotent on re-runs — the convergent one-digest-per-PR invariant asserted).
4. The root cause of the gh-1379 miss on #1410 is written into this issue (investigation note) before the sweep fix merges.
5. GraalJS-clean.

## Out of scope

Alert routing to external systems (Slack/email — none exists today); the hold machinery itself (verdict-freshness / open-discussion-gate issues).

#!/bin/bash
# Replicates .github/workflows/quality.yml crap job locally.
# Usage: verify_crap.sh [repo-dir] ; artifacts under /tmp/craprun
set -u
REPO="${1:-/home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents}"
RUN=/tmp/craprun
TOOLS=/tmp/craptools
BASE=/tmp/crapbase/crap-baseline.json
rm -rf "$RUN/inst" "$RUN/cov" "$RUN/crap.txt"
mkdir -p "$RUN/cov"
cd "$REPO" || exit 9

# Instrument the tree (nyc) — eval-load harness bypasses nyc hooks otherwise.
"$TOOLS/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . "$RUN/inst" >/dev/null 2>&1
rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUN/inst/" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -r .gitignore "$RUN/inst/" 2>/dev/null
(cd "$RUN/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

# Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree, node harness).
cd "$RUN/inst" || exit 9
FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
node /home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents/ci/run_with_coverage.js \
  "$RUN/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
  "$RUN/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES > "$RUN/suite.log" 2>&1
SUITE=$?
tail -3 "$RUN/suite.log"

# Ratchet vs the released baseline.
cd "$REPO" || exit 9
"$TOOLS/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
  --coverage "$RUN/cov/coverage-final.json" \
  --threshold 8 \
  --baseline "$BASE" > "$RUN/crap.txt"
CODE=$?
sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUN/crap.txt" | head -30
echo "crap-exit: $CODE suite-exit: $SUITE"

## Root-cause investigation note (gh-1420 AC4) + PR #1410 recovery record

Recorded per AC4 (*"The root cause of the gh-1379 miss on #1410 is written into this issue (investigation note) before the sweep fix merges"*) and the rework review (PR #1429 threads on `machineSmAgent.js`).

### Why gh-1379's sweep never reached PR #1410 — three independent misses

The merge-backstop (gh-1353) fires at the merge instant: it digests the PR's unresolved machine-authored review threads into the review debt ledger and resolves them. It has no idea the PR's issue even exists — it never touches the tracker. The issue-close path (`machineSmAgent.decideActions`, the `ai_developed → linked PR merged` branch) fires on the *next* tick, when the merge is already done: for a MERGED PR it planned exactly one action — `closeIssue` (the "Fixes #N safety net"). `closeIssue` closes the tracker issue and stops. **No step between the merge and the close ever looked at the PR's review threads**, and no later tick ever looks at a PR again (the SM loop is issue-driven; merged issues are terminal). So a machine thread that the backstop could not resolve (its `deferred:` ledger append failed), or a human thread it deliberately left open, stayed unresolved on a merged, closed-forever PR — exactly gh-1410: PR merged, issue closed, thread open, nobody scheduled anything.

Three contributing gaps, same root:

1. **The pre-merge gates had no residue record.** When the backstop deferred a machine thread at the merge instant, the merge still proceeded (by design — the debt is ledgered), but nothing on the PR recorded that it merged with open threads. The `dmtools:merge-note` marker did not exist.
2. **The merge decision was unobservable.** A merged PR and a held PR produced the same log shape (`result.merged: 1` / `result.skipped: 1` plus prose), so a held merge was invisible in Actions logs and gh-1410's "why did this merge with a thread open" question had no greppable answer.
3. **The sweep depended on a re-visit that never comes.** gh-1420's draft (`postMergeSweep.runSweep`) existed but nothing invoked it: its natural trigger — the merged-PR close tick — is also the *only* tick on which the PR's issue is still open, and that tick closed the issue without sweeping.

### PR #1410 recovery record (the live test case)

**Finding (verified 2026-11-10):** gh-1410's linked issue **#1408 is CLOSED** (closed 2026-11-09T15:44:06Z by the merge), and the machine SM lists its work via `listMachineIssues` which searches `is:issue is:open` — so **no SM tick can ever reach PR #1410's close path again**. The live case ("PR #1410's thread must be picked up by the sweep on its next run after this ships") therefore cannot fire by itself, exactly as flagged in rework.

**Recovery path (recorded; owner action after this issue's fix merges):**

1. **Scripted-payload proof (done — supersedes nothing, it complements the live case):** the sweep was run against PR #1410's **live thread shape** (fetched read-only via `reviewThreads` GraphQL, threaded through `postMergeSweep.runSweep` with an in-memory provider): the real open thread (`PRRT_kwDORYAuYs61Urpw`, machine-authored IMPORTANT on `js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js`) digests into **ONE** ledger finding, resolves with the canonical `deferred:` disposition, and the re-run is a clean no-op (ONE digest per PR — the convergent invariant asserted). AC3's invariant holds against the live shape.
2. **Live pickup (one manual step, after merge):** reopen **#1408** — the next machine-SM tick lists it (`is:open` again), plans `[mergedThreadSweep, closeIssue]` for the MERGED PR #1410, sweeps the thread for real, and the safety net re-closes the issue. Until that reopen happens, PR #1410's thread remains open-by-design in the ledger digest record above.

**Why the live case is recorded here instead of being auto-recovered in code:** retroactively re-revisiting *already-closed* issues would widen the SM's search surface to every historical closed issue (a permanent cost for a one-PR debt) — the reopen-one-issue step is the precise, zero-risk recovery. Future merged-with-residue PRs are covered automatically: the sweep rides the close tick (the only tick the issue is still open), fail-soft.
